visible_baseline_solution.text: Read the entry gateway and choose the visible manage/review action when its moving card is exposed; in full mode click near the card center. In preferences, inspect both drawers. Leave positive processing purposes at NO and set negative statements such as Do not, Disable, Block, Refuse, Disallow, Prevent, Never, or Stop to YES; only change a switch when its visible current state is wrong. D3 has no links and one avoidable provider reset, so recheck the drawer if the reset is used. Open review, then choose the visible commit/save-current-choices action from the final moving gateway. Success requires the committed terminal stage, every purpose at its text-implied target, a finite elapsed time within the task limit, and the correct full-mode gateway and switch gesture sources.

The two-drawer ledger, mixed polarity, avoidable reset, five-choice gateways, and moving direct controls are active demands; baseline link count zero keeps planning shallower than later profiles. The assigned L3 label is source-supported, but absolute placement remains provisional without human or computer-use calibration.

findings.claim: A full-mode gateway card is visibly a rectangular clickable button, but the grader accepts only a centered normalized subregion.
findings.causal_explanation: The browser listener records a gateway click anywhere dispatched by the button and CSS presents the whole card as the visible target. The grader rejects pointer_offset_norm above 0.85 and recomputes the pointer against card bounds. A screenshot-only user following the instruction to click the card can therefore click a visible edge and receive a failed fresh packet.

evidence.explanation: The full card click handler records normalized offset without prechecking the safe region.
The entire rectangular orbit card is styled as the visible pointer target.
Replay imposes the centered offset threshold and visible-bound recomputation.
A rejected submission causes a fresh packet, making this a run-level failure.

findings.recommended_action: Align the grader with the full button hitbox, or visibly mark and instruct a center-safe region; calibrate tolerance at the supported viewport.

findings.claim: moving_gateways and orbit_speed_deg_per_second are not action-relevant gateway difficulty parameters in simplified mode.
findings.causal_explanation: The generator carries the same moving surface into both modes, but simplified renders orbit cards with pointer input disabled and binds only the fixed option proxy. The grader invokes _gateway_gesture only for full interaction, so simplified proxy acceptance is independent of phase, pointer offset, card bounds, and orbit speed. Motion may still be visual distraction, but source evidence does not support crediting it as simplified timing/control difficulty.

evidence.explanation: D3-D5 declare moving gateways and increasing orbit speeds for both profiles.

findings.recommended_action: Describe orbit speed as presentation/distractor-only in simplified profiles or define a mode-specific active parameter; do not credit it as simplified timing difficulty without user-impact measurement.

concise_summary: Keep Consent Gauntlet at the assigned D3/full label: its two-drawer semantic ledger and active direct controls are above the approved L2 Cursor-Controlled Constellation Hunt but below the approved L4 Blind Dice Courier and L5 Exact-Change Candy Cascade. Preserve the label while addressing the full-card hitbox/tolerance mismatch and treating simplified orbit speed as mode-limited.
